title: Ajisai MCP result
description: One envelope for every Ajisai MCP tool result (compute, check, infer_contracts, word_contract). `status` separates the three outcomes the boundary keeps distinct: a successful run (which includes a reason-carrying NIL), an Ajisai language error carrying its `message` and `error`, and a failure of the host rather than of the program. An optional field carrying no value is omitted rather than sent as `null`, so `message` and `error` are simply absent from a plain success, and `contractDecls` from a source that declares no contract — test for presence, not for `null`. The text content block of a tool result carries this same object serialized, so a text-only client receives the whole result and not a summary of it.

specificationVersion.description: The specification version the engine implements, as the engine's own envelope states it. During the beta a program's answer can change when it does; spec/CHANGELOG.md in the Ajisai repository names each change. Carried once, here, beside `mcp.engineVersion`'s release number.

stackElided.description: Present when the stack was too large to send in full and the values of the slots that do not fit a byte budget were dropped; this record says which. On an `error` the budget is the fixed one every error report applies (`errorStackBudget`): the report's answer is its error, and the stack is residual state. On an `ok` it is the agent profile's stack budget (`valueStackBudget`): the values that fit arrive whole, and an oversized one arrives as this record rather than the whole result being refused as `responseTooLarge`, so a caller learns what it left on the stack and can fix the program. Absent whenever nothing was dropped, which is every ordinary result.

slots.description: One entry per dropped slot, in stack order.

index.description: Position in `stack` and `stackDisplay`. Slots keep their index: a dropped slot is replaced in place, never removed, so an index still points at the same thing.

approxBytes.description: Roughly what the slot would have serialized to, counted without building the text.

elements.description: Direct children, for a collection. Absent for a leaf.

outcome.description: compute only. Which of the language’s three results (LANG.FAILURE) the run produced, as a spec/outcomes.json id: `value`, `nil:<reason>` for a reasoned absence on top of the stack (still `status: ok`), or `error:<category>` for a language ERROR (`status: error`, whose `error.category` is the same category). Absent only when the result cannot be classified (an unlabelled NIL, an error naming no category).

inputs.description: Values the Word consumes, or `variable` where the data decides.

outputs.description: Values the Word leaves, or `variable` where the data decides.

field.description: LANG.CONTRACT.FIELD: `leaving` when the body can answer a point over zero (`1/0` or `0/0`) from operands holding none — a DIV, POW or NUM whose operands can reach past the field, a literal over zero, or code the inference cannot read — and `closed` otherwise, in which case the field laws hold over finite operands. A `DIV` by a divisor that cannot be zero (`2 DIV`, `2 SQRT DIV`, `LENGTH 1 ADD DIV`) or a `POW` to an exponent that cannot be negative stays `closed`.

fieldExits.description: Where a `leaving` body leaves the field, in body order: the Words it calls there and the literals it writes over zero. Empty for a `closed` body.

suggested.description: A paste-ready `#:contract` line for this Word (`#:contract W inputs=N outputs=N field=closed|leaving`), so pasting it back verifies exactly what was reported.

contracts.description: Inferred contracts for the user-defined Words in the submitted source (`infer_contracts` only). `inputs`, `outputs` and `field` are spelled as in the Record `CONTRACT` answers inside the language, so an inferred and a registered contract compare directly.

prelude.description: The phrasebook Words a `words` argument defined before `source` ran, in the order they ran, each with its content digest (`[ NAME ] 0 GET DIGEST`), which matches the `#:digest` line of ajisai://phrasebook. Absent when the call named no `words`.

resourceUsage.description: What this run spent of the budgets that could have refused it. Every key names a ceiling of the `ajisai://limits` profile (`mcp.limitProfile`) and carries the same number the ceiling compared against — read from the counter the check reads, not a parallel copy — so an agent can subtract one from the other and know what it has left. The accumulating ceilings always appear. `algebraicTerms` is a per-result ceiling, so it reports the largest term count any result of the run reached — the number that ceiling compared — and only when some result was an irrational.

numericWork.description: Internal arithmetic work charged, in limb-multiply units, against the `numericWork` ceiling.

collectionWork.description: Element operations charged inside collection Words — copies, order comparisons and equality probes — against the `collectionWork` ceiling. Priced from the operand, so an element that is wide, nested or algebraic costs more than a machine word; a collection Word loops inside one execution step, so this is the only counter that can see it.

algebraicTerms.description: The largest number of algebraic terms one result of the run carried, against the `algebraicTerms` ceiling. Absent when no result was an irrational. A Word whose charge grows with it marks that axis `valueDependent` in its `word_contract` entry.

message.description: On an `error`, what went wrong, as one line of text. Absent from a success.

contractDecls.description: check only, and only when the source declares a `#:contract` (`#:contract W inputs=N outputs=N field=closed|leaving`). Each declaration is compared with the contract inferred for its Word; a contradiction, or a malformed directive, is an `error` finding and makes the report a `contractViolation` error.

outcome.description: The worst outcome among the declarations: `error` when any is contradicted or malformed, `nil` when one cannot be verified, `value` when every one holds.

error.description: On `status: error`, the language error (`languageError`); on `status: hostError`, the host failure (`hostError`). Absent from a success.

registrySchemaVersion.description: Schema version of the packaged Word registry (`word_contract` only). Distinct from the envelope's own `schemaVersion`.

matches.description: Canonical registry entries matching the requested Word (`word_contract` only).

suggestions.description: Registry names closest to an unmatched request, best match first (`word_contract` only). Empty whenever `matches` is non-empty.

serverVersion.description: Version of this MCP adapter — a separate component from the Ajisai engine below it. A stored result names both, so a missing field can be told apart from a field this adapter version never sent.

assetDigest.description: SHA-256 of the Word registry file this adapter packages (assets/words.json), checked against assets/metadata.json at startup. It identifies the adapter's asset, not the engine.

backend.description: Which of the two interchangeable backends answered. They are semantically equivalent — `backend/parity-test.js` asserts it case by case — so this identifies the execution path for auditing, not a difference in meaning.

limitProfile.description: The name of the host profile applied to this call — the `profile` of the `ajisai://limits` resource, which carries the twelve ceilings themselves. They are constants of the server, so they travel once, in that resource, rather than on every result; a ceiling that fires names itself in `error.resource` and its value in `message`, and a host failure about one names it in `error.limit`. Every entry is pinned by a case in `golden/limits.json`.

languageError.description: An Ajisai language ERROR, never a failure of the host. Branch on `category`; `message` beside it is the text.

category.description: The spec/outcomes.json error category — the id `outcome` names as `error:<category>`.

resource.description: For `resourceLimitExceeded`, the ceiling crossed — an entry of the `ajisai://limits` profile.

word.description: The Word the failure is attributed to.

hostError.description: A failure of the host, never of the Ajisai program. `code` is the stable identifier to branch on; `message` is safe to show a model and deliberately carries no host paths, environment-variable names or spawn detail.

limit.description: The declared ceiling (an entry of `ajisai://limits`) this failure is about, when it is about one.

wordContract.description: One canonical entry of the generated `spec/words.json` registry, reproduced verbatim.

purity.description: `pure`, `conditional` or `effectful` (spec/words.schema.json). `conditional` is a Word that runs a code block it is given (`MAP`, `FILTER`, `FOLD`, `SCAN`, `EXEC`): it has that block's effects and no others, so it is pure exactly when the block is.

cost.description: What the Word charges on each of the three metered resources the runtime counts (`executionSteps` / `numericWork` / `collectionWork`). The classes join pointwise under concatenation, so a phrase's bound on an axis is the widest class any of its Words declares there — which is what lets a caller budget a program without running it.

field.description: `closed` when every number the Word answers lies in the field whenever every number it reads does; `leaving` when it can answer a point over zero (`1/0`, `0/0`) from operands that hold none (LANG.CONTRACT.FIELD). The same key a `#:contract` declaration takes as `field=closed|leaving`.

exactTerm.description: One term c·√m of the normal form: the rational coefficient numerator/denominator and the square-free radicand m (1 for the rational term).

protocolNode.description: One stack value as observed at the host boundary. Every field is derived from the value itself, never from the Word that produced it (LANG.VALUES.DENOTATION). A vector's own elements are observedValue nodes in turn (see `value` below), so this definition is recursive.

type.description: The value's domain (LANG.VALUES.DISJOINT), discriminating `value`'s shape. A NIL is `nil` wherever it stands, including in truth position, where it reads as UNKNOWN (LANG.VALUES.TRUTH).

value.description: Shape depends on `type`: nil -> null; boolean -> boolean; number -> {numerator, denominator} (arbitrary-precision decimal strings, the pair reduced and the denominator non-negative: zero exactly for the two points over zero, `1/0` and `0/0`, LANG.VALUES.EXACT); string or symbol -> string (a symbol's bare name); vector -> an array of observedValue; record -> {keys, values}, two arrays of observedValue of equal length, aligned position by position (LANG.RECORDS.STRUCTURE). null for any type when `elided` is present.

costAxis.description: A sound upper bound on one metered resource. `class` bounds how the charge grows with the Word's input; `exact` records that some contribution provably attains it, rather than the bound being a safe over-approximation.

valueDependent.description: Present when this axis's charge also grows with an algebraic operand's term count, which `class` cannot see. Set by measurement.

protocolSemantics.description: Present on every node, a Vector nested in a Vector included: how a value is stored does not decide what its node says (LANG.AUTHORITY.FREEDOM). Every field is optional. Both host surfaces emit the same set, because both render it with one function (rust/src/agent/report.rs::semantics_json).

truthValue.description: Present on a Boolean node, and only there (rust/src/types/value_absence.rs::truth_value). UNKNOWN is a NIL (LANG.VALUES.TRUTH) and is observed through `absence`, not here.

approximate.description: true when the node is an irrational scalar (LANG.VALUES.EXACT), whose `value` is therefore a rational approximation: the best convergent the observation budget affords, or, for a value too large to afford even one, a term-by-term one. `exactTerms` is the value. Never present otherwise.

exactTerms.description: An irrational scalar's exact multiquadratic normal form, structured for computation: one term per {numerator, denominator, radicand}. The stack display writes the same terms as one token (`sqrt(2)`, `1/1+sqrt(2)`).

protocolAbsence.description: Present only on a nil-type node. `reason` is the stable, machine-readable identifier LANG.VALUES.NIL calls the entire observable content of a NIL (one of spec/outcomes.json's NIL reasons); it is absent only for a NIL an implementation could not yet label. `detail` is the text a `userDeclared` reason carries, which is part of that reason.

protocolElided.description: Present only in the stack of a CLI/MCP agent report, on a slot whose value was dropped to keep the report deliverable (rust/src/agent/error_stack.rs): under the fixed error budget every error report applies (`errorStackBudget`), or under the stack budget a host chose for successful results (`valueStackBudget`, the agent profile's; the trusted profile sets none). `type` and `semantics` still describe what the value was (less an algebraic value's `exactTerms`, whose count moves here); `value` is null. Tell it apart from a genuine NIL by `type`, which names the real domain, and by this field's presence.

protocolTruncated.description: Present only in the playground's stack view (AjisaiInterpreter.collect_stack, rust/src/agent/stack_view.rs), on a vector cut to its first 100 elements, the most the playground draws of one collection; never in a CLI/MCP agent report. `value` holds those leading elements, each a full observedValue (cut in turn if it is a long vector). This field describes what was left out, so a host decides from the view what it would decide from the whole value: `length` is the vector's element count; `holdsNil` and `holdsRecord` say whether a NIL or a Record sits anywhere in the left-out elements; `digest` is a 64-bit hash of the left-out elements under value equality, so the views of two different values differ. Presentation only: the value on the stack stays whole.
